# Limits

Source: <https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/limits>

We set four limits for each partner. Until we agree different values with you, the defaults below apply. [Ask us](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/support) to change them.

| Limit | Default | What it counts |
|---|---|---|
| Requests per second | 20, with bursts up to 40 | Every request made with any of your keys, counted together. |
| Requests in progress at once | 5 | `POST /v1/orders`, `POST /v1/orders/estimate`, `DELETE /v1/orders/{id}`, `POST /v1/applications`, `PUT /v1/applications/{id}/documents/{type}` and `POST /v1/allocations`, across all your keys. |
| Order value per day | ₦10,000,000 | The value of the orders you place in one day, West Africa Time (WAT). |
| Allocations per day | ₦50,000,000 | The amount you allocate in one day, WAT. |

## When you reach a limit

| Limit | Response | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Requests per second | `429 rate_limited`, with `Retry-After: 1` | Wait 1 second, then send the same request again. For a request that takes an `Idempotency-Key`, keep the same key. |
| Requests in progress at once | `429 rate_limited`, with `Retry-After: 1` | Wait 1 second, then send the same request again. For a request that takes an `Idempotency-Key`, keep the same key. |
| Order value per day | `422 limit_exceeded` | Nothing was stored, so the key is still free. The limit resets at midnight, WAT. A single order larger than the whole daily limit never fits: split it, or [ask us](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/support) to change the limit. |
| Allocations per day | `422 limit_exceeded` | Nothing was stored, so the key is still free. The limit resets at midnight, WAT. A single allocation larger than the whole daily limit never fits: split it, or [ask us](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/support) to change the limit. |

We refuse these requests before we store or send anything. `Retry-After` is the only rate limit header we send today.

## See what's left

`GET /v1/limits` returns each limit, what you've used of it and what's left, counted exactly as the limit counts it. For the two daily limits, `resets_at` says when the count starts again. `remaining` is what one more request can use at that moment: another of your requests can use it first.

## How order value is counted

Each order counts when you place it, at its quantity times a price per share:

| Order | Price per share |
|---|---|
| Limit buy | Its `price_kobo`. |
| Any other order | The day's upper price limit for the symbol, which we ask the broker for when you place the order. Nothing trades above it. |

How much of an order still counts depends on its state:

| State | Counts |
|---|---|
| `refused` | Nothing. It never reached the exchange. |
| `rejected`, `cancelled`, `expired` | Only the shares that filled before it ended. |
| Any other state, including `uncertain` | The whole order. |

## How allocations are counted

Every allocation created that day counts, except `rejected` and `refused` ones, whose amounts return to your wallet.

## Fixed limits

These are the same for every partner.

| What | Limit | Response |
|---|---|---|
| Request body | 16 KiB | `413 request_too_large` |
| A document's body, `PUT /v1/applications/{id}/documents/{type}` | Less than 1,000,000 bytes, arriving within 30 seconds | `413 document_too_large`; a body slower than that, `400 invalid_request` |
| Documents on their way to the broker at once | 2 of yours, 4 across all partners | `429 rate_limited`, with `Retry-After: 1`, before the body is read |
| `quantity` on an order | 1 to 100,000,000 shares | `400 invalid_request`, with `param` set to `quantity` |
| `price_kobo` on a limit order | 1 to 1,000,000,000 kobo (₦10,000,000 a share) | `400 invalid_request`, with `param` set to `price_kobo` |
| `symbol` | 20 characters: letters, digits, dots and hyphens | `400 invalid_request`, with `param` set to `symbol` |
| `amount_kobo` on one allocation | 1 to 10,000,000,000 kobo (₦100,000,000) | `400 invalid_request`, with `param` set to `amount_kobo` |
| Each application field | 200 characters | `400 invalid_request`, with `param` naming the field |
| `Idempotency-Key` | 255 characters | `400 invalid_request`, with `param` set to `Idempotency-Key` |
| `limit` on a list | 1 to 100, default 25 | `400 invalid_request`, with `param` set to `limit` |
| Trades or contract notes in one request | 1,000 records | `400 invalid_request`, with `param` set to `from`. Ask for a shorter date range. |
| `POST /v1/keys/revoke` from one address (an IPv6 /64 counts as one address) | 5 a second, with bursts up to 10 | `429 rate_limited`, with `Retry-After: 1` |

## How long a request can take

| What | Time |
|---|---|
| The longest `POST /v1/orders` takes to answer | 95 seconds |
| The longest any request stays open | 115 seconds. We close the connection then. |
| Your client timeout | More than 115 seconds |

A request with no answer by then has timed out. For a request that takes an `Idempotency-Key`, send it again with the same key.

## Reads that ask the broker

Balances, positions, trades, contract notes and the reference lists are read from the broker each time you ask. Each partner can have 2 of these reads in progress at once, and at most 4 run at once across all partners, so other partners' reads can delay yours. A read that can't start and finish within 20 seconds returns `503 exchange_unavailable`. Nothing was changed. Send the request again, [backing off](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/handle-errors#4-back-off-between-retries) between attempts.

Avoid reading the broker each time a customer opens your app. Keep your own copy of each account's balance and positions, refresh it when an event changes the account, such as a fill or a booked allocation, and read the broker when you need the latest figure, such as before a sell.
